prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create actual newly illustrated 2D game animation frame artwork, not a preview board. The supplied PNG is the approved character design and painting style reference, not an image to rotate, scale, squash, warp or reuse as a cutout. Draw every pose afresh with coherent anatomy, newly drawn contours, material surfaces and lighting appropriate to that pose. Polished soft hand-painted 2D sprite shading, fine dark teal outline, warm upper-left light, exactly match the reference palette and visual finish. One sprite sheet only: exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 equal square cells, read left to right then top to bottom. Requested output 2048x2048 pixels. Genuinely transparent background, NO checkerboard drawing, NO scene, ground, backdrop, shadows, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines, cell borders, glow or extra characters. No object crosses its cell boundary. Fixed camera, fixed drawing scale and fixed ground baseline at 88% of each cell. On the first frame the character is centered horizontally, full neutral visible height about 60% of a cell, from 28% to 88%; keep its mass and scale consistent, let only the actual death action change its silhouette. This is a one-shot DEATH followed by still remains, never return to life. Design the intervening drawings as sequential animation poses, not sixteen unrelated variations. All 16 cells must contain the same recognizable character at successive moments of the action. Character: the reference translucent turquoise water spirit, NO feet and NO limbs. Broad teardrop-shaped liquid body with a very distinctive upper wave curling toward the right, pale mint interior light and deep teal edge, two dark blue eyes low on the main body. Preserve this silhouette and aquatic identity initially. Death action: first the upper curl loses its surface tension and pours into the main body, then the remaining body pours outward into a low broad puddle; a small last concentric surface ripple settles to stillness. Draw the actual liquid physics and new surface/outline in each pose, NOT a flattened or scaled copy of the original standing spirit. Redraw flowing fluid folds, curving little crest turning into the body, changing highlights and broad elliptical surface. No separate rigid upside-down teardrop shape should survive in the puddle. Row 1 frames 1-4: neutral standing, eyes gently close, curl relaxes and folds forward and down, a wave of liquid rolls down the shoulder. Row 2 frames 5-8: upper wave pours into the main body and vanishes, shoulders melt, fluid flows out along the ground as body lowers, eyes fade and are gone before the puddle. Row 3 frames 9-12: body becomes a genuinely drawn shallow glossy turquoise pool with rounded spreading edges, one small ring wave travels across its surface. Row 4 frames 13-16: successive diminishing concentric surface rings, then a completely still broad rounded puddle. The final pool stays opaque enough to read, soft blue-green depth shading and a quiet pale highlight, no face and no remnant curl. It retains the same total character identity/color and apparent liquid mass. Keep the pool entirely within the cell, max width 82% of a cell. No splash airborne drops, particles, vapor, magic or fade to nothing. Fixed floor contact throughout, no hopping. Last frame is still water remains.
